actions.definition: Two unit actions through the same forward function, the roster as signed: hire one AE starting 2026-09-01; add $1,000,000 of program pipeline starting 2026-09-01. Gain per dollar is the bookings gained in the next twelve months over the cash cost inside the same twelve months. An action starts paying in the first month it adds at least 1% of its twelve-month gain.
actions.meaning: 'feasible' means achievable inside the model's bounds, not operationally achievable; that a new hire adds pipeline at the fitted rate is an assumption

ranges.method: Each side's factor is the ceil(90% of n)-th smallest of the factors the n eligible past forecasts would have needed: the plain empirical rule, not a finite-sample guarantee. Six-month factors come from overlapping forecasts (each shares five of its six months with its neighbors) and are noisier: 11 past six-month forecasts to learn from, 1 scored.
ranges.reason: pooled over 1 and 3 months, 18 scored folds: simulated 16 held (89%), stretched 16 held (89%); the stretched coverage is not closer to 80%
ranges.rule: adopted if there are at least 6 scored folds at 1 and at 3 months, pooled 80% coverage over 1 and 3 months is closer to 80% than the simulated range's on the same folds, and no horizon (1, 3 or 6 months) moves more than 10 points further from 80%; each side's factor is the smallest, never below 1, that would have put at least 90% of the eligible past folds inside on that side (a fold is eligible once its whole horizon has ended; at least 5 are needed)

recency.reason: mean absolute error not lower at both 1 and 3 months (1m: 140,113 vs 96,781; 3m: 299,207 vs 269,872)
recency.rule: adopted only if the fitted model's mean absolute error is lower than the Goal 1 fit's at both 1 and 3 months, on the same folds (at least 6 at each)

backtest.reason: the model's mean absolute error is lower than both baselines at 1 and 3 months
backtest.scoring: per horizon, mean absolute dollar error over all folds; 'yes' only if the fitted model's error is lower than both baselines at 1 and 3 months; under 6 folds is 'not enough history to say'

driver_actions.definition: A driver action is a named change to one driver in one slice, with a start month, a ramp and a target. It changes the pipeline created from its start, ramping linearly by creation date to the target and holding it after. Pipeline created before the start, and every deal already open, keeps the rates it had. Where the capacity term is in use, hires and programs stay as the plan has them; each action is valued against them. For a segment, the target is an entered change on the pooled baseline win rate, not a win rate that was measured for the segment.
driver_actions.line: An action changes the win rate of pipeline created from its start month on. Deals already open keep their odds. A segment's target is an entered change on the pooled baseline, not a measured segment rate.

worksheet.expectation_note: Every figure here is an expected value from the forward function. No simulation is run, so no range is attached to any sensitivity.
worksheet.history_note: Historical settings describe what the company has done. They are not forecasts, they are not called achievable, and nothing here says they will happen again.
worksheet.measured_around: the plan in force: its hires and program pipeline, as applied
worksheet.sensitivity_note: Each change is a conditional change in expected bookings, measured one driver at a time around the plan in force. It is not a forecast and not a cause, and the bars are never summed: drivers act together, not alone.
